The episode instantiates the expectations-asymmetry mechanism the prediction names: a single custom-ASIC vendor's merely-solid quarter repriced the whole group because these names are priced for continuous beat-and-raise. What remains for confirmation is the same pattern on the next in-line print accompanied by visible sell-side estimate cuts or a group re-rating.

prediction_ref.short_label: Coding-agent frameworks ship goal-grounded completion verification by H1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: This prediction originates today and lands directly on its source. The DeployBench arxiv benchmark (2606.05238, submitted June 3) is a 51-task research-artifact-deployment suite where an agent must stand up a paper's released code on a fresh machine - resolving multi-language toolchains, GPU/CUDA, kernel configuration, and legacy compatibility. Four state-of-the-art LLMs inside the OpenHands harness scored only 7.8% to 51.0%, and the dominant failure mode was a 'completion-judgment problem': agent-terminated self-stops where the agent's own pre-finish checks declared success against a weaker or different target than the task required. That isolates verification - not raw capability - as the binding constraint, and because the failure is a property of the harness rather than the model, it is fixable at the framework layer. The prediction is that frameworks make goal-grounded completion verification a default by H1 2027; today supplies the motivating measurement, with shipped framework features still to come.

prediction_ref.short_label: Token-drift trajectory probes land as agentic-coherence audit primitive by Q4 2026

validation_rows.evidence_summary: DeployBench surfaces exactly the failure class this prediction expects audit tooling to target. Its dominant error mode - a 'completion-judgment problem' where agents self-stop after their own pre-finish checks declare success against a weaker or different target than the task requires - is an agentic-coherence breakdown: the agent's internal sense of 'done' has drifted away from the real goal. A 51-task suite across four state-of-the-art models (pass rates 7.8% to 51.0%) quantifies how common that drift is and frames it as the binding constraint on autonomous deployment, strengthening the case for trajectory-level probes that monitor whether an agent's run stays anchored to its objective. The remaining gap is that DeployBench measures the problem rather than shipping the token-drift trajectory-probe primitive itself as a standardized agentic-coherence audit.
